questions.question_english: Which of the following actions constitutes a violation of Section 17 (Prohibition of physical punishment and mental harassment)?
options_english: Making a student stand outside in the sun as punishment.
Evaluating a student's academic answer sheet strictly according to marking guidelines
Reporting a student's continuous absence to the parents
Providing additional remedial homework to a weak student
questions.explanation_english: Section 17 forbids physical punishment and mental harassment. Subjecting a child to physical strain or heat by forcing them to stand outside in the sun constitutes physical punishment and cruel treatment, directly violating statutory child protection provisions.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विद्यार्थी को दंडस्वरूप धूप में खड़ा रखना है। धारा 17 शारीरिक दंड और मानसिक उत्पीड़न को प्रतिबंधित करती है। तेज धूप में दंडस्वरूप खड़ा करना शारीरिक कष्ट या अपमानजनक दंड बन सकता है। उत्तर-पुस्तिका का निष्पक्ष मूल्यांकन, माता-पिता को अनुपस्थिति की सूचना देना और सीखने की जरूरत के अनुरूप उपचारात्मक गृहकार्य देना अपने आप में इस निषेध का उल्लंघन नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Making a student stand outside in the sun as punishment.

Section 17 forbids physical punishment and mental harassment. Subjecting a child to physical strain or heat by forcing them to stand outside in the sun constitutes physical punishment and cruel treatment, directly violating statutory child protection provisions.

questions.question_english: Which is the most appropriate action for a State Government if its existing schools do not meet the PTR norms stipulated in the RTE Act upon its commencement?
options_english: Close the non-compliant schools immediately until adequate teaching staff is recruited.
Stop all new student admissions completely until the required number of regular teachers are hired.
Ensure PTR norms are met within three years of commencement.
Formally request a permanent statutory exemption from the Central Government for non-compliant schools.
questions.explanation_english: Section 25 mandated that within three years from the commencement of the Act, the appropriate government and local authorities had to ensure that the Pupil-Teacher Ratio specified in the Schedule was maintained across all schools under their administrative control, requiring strategic teacher recruitment and rationalized deployment without closing non-compliant institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर तीन वर्ष के भीतर PTR मानदंड पूरे करना सुनिश्चित करना है। अधिनियम और उसकी अनुसूची विद्यालयों के लिए न्यूनतम शिक्षक मानक निर्धारित करते हैं तथा अनुपालन के लिए समय-सीमा का प्रावधान करते हैं। विद्यालयों को तत्काल बंद करना या सभी प्रवेश रोक देना अधिनियम की सामान्य आवश्यकता नहीं है। राज्य सरकार को आवश्यक शिक्षक नियुक्त करके निर्धारित अवधि में मानक हासिल करने की योजना बनानी चाहिए।

questions.question_english: A parent complains to the local authority that their child was beaten by a teacher. The local authority fails to respond within three months. What is the next statutory recourse available to the parent under the RTE grievance mechanism?
options_english: Appeal to the SCPCR.
File a formal police FIR against the school under the provisions of the RTE Act.
Appeal to the School Management Committee requesting the immediate termination of the teacher.
Organize a community boycott of the school until the complaint is resolved.
questions.explanation_english: Section 32 provides that any person aggrieved by a decision of the local authority, or by its failure to decide a complaint within the prescribed three-month timeframe, has the statutory right to prefer an appeal directly to the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR).
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर SCPCR के समक्ष अपील करना है। RTE अधिनियम के अंतर्गत स्थानीय प्राधिकारी शिकायत पर तीन महीने के भीतर निर्णय करता है। यदि वह निर्धारित अवधि में निर्णय नहीं देता, तो शिकायतकर्ता को राज्य बाल अधिकार संरक्षण आयोग या लागू अपीलीय व्यवस्था के समक्ष जाने का उपाय उपलब्ध है। पुलिस शिकायत अलग कानूनी प्रक्रिया हो सकती है, लेकिन प्रश्न RTE की वैधानिक शिकायत-निवारण प्रक्रिया पूछता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Appeal to the SCPCR.

Section 7 provides that the Central Government and State Governments share concurrent financial responsibility for implementing the statutory provisions. questions.question_english: Consider the case of an un-aided private school that refuses to establish a School Management Committee. What is the legal implication?

questions.explanation_english: Section 21 explicitly exempts private unaided non-minority schools from the mandatory requirement to form a School Management Committee. Therefore, an unaided private school operates legally without a Section 21 SMC, remaining governed by its trust management and state-prescribed parent-teacher bodies.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। धारा 21 के अंतर्गत SMC गठन का अनिवार्य प्रावधान सरकारी और सहायता-प्राप्त विद्यालयों पर लागू होता है; निजी गैर-सहायता-प्राप्त विद्यालयों को इस विशिष्ट अनिवार्यता से छूट है। इसलिए केवल SMC न बनाने के कारण उनकी मान्यता स्वतः वापस नहीं ली जाती। यह छूट अधिनियम के अन्य लागू प्रावधानों से मुक्त होने का अर्थ नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The school is operating legally, as unaided private schools are exempted from Section 21 (SMC formation) under the RTE Act.

Assertion (A): The Central Government has a statutory duty to develop a national framework of curriculum under the RTE Act.
Reason (R): State Governments lack the academic expertise and financial resources to develop curriculum frameworks at the elementary level.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.explanation_english: The Central Government is statutorily empowered under the RTE Act to specify an academic authority that will lay down the curriculum and evaluation procedure for elementary education. The assertion is therefore correct. The reason is incorrect: the Act does not say that State Governments lack academic expertise or financial resources. States have academic bodies such as SCERTs and retain important responsibilities for adapting and implementing curricular arrangements within the national framework. A national-level role and state-level capacity can coexist; the existence of the former does not establish the alleged incapacity in the reason.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प C है। RTE अधिनियम के अंतर्गत केंद्र सरकार को राष्ट्रीय पाठ्यचर्या रूपरेखा से जुड़ी भूमिका दी गई है, लेकिन कारण में दिया गया दावा कि राज्य सरकारों के पास विशेषज्ञता और संसाधन नहीं हैं, अधिनियम का वैधानिक आधार नहीं है। राष्ट्रीय समन्वय और शैक्षिक प्राधिकारियों की भूमिका निर्धारित करना अलग बात है; राज्यों की क्षमता के बारे में व्यापक नकारात्मक निष्कर्ष निकालना अलग। इसलिए अभिकथन सही और कारण गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) A is true but R is false

The Central Government is statutorily empowered under the RTE Act to specify an academic authority that will lay down the curriculum and evaluation procedure for elementary education. The assertion is therefore correct. The reason is incorrect: the Act does not say that State Governments lack academic expertise or financial resources. States have academic bodies such as SCERTs and retain important responsibilities for adapting and implementing curricular arrangements within the national framework. A national-level role and state-level capacity can coexist; the existence of the former does not establish the alleged incapacity in the reason.
